title: Shooting inquest continues in Terrace
article: A man who failed to show up in court to face criminal charges is now the subject of an inquest in Terrace after that man ended up shot in the back.
On Wednesday an officer who was there testified he heard his fellow officers order the suspect to drop his weapon, and then, right away, heard eight shots fired in rapid succession.
The only non-RCMP witness to the shooting of Rodney Shayne Jackson, 35, is his brother, and so far he has given no indication that he will testify at this coroner's inquest.
However, an ambulance attendant who spoke to Jackson's brother hours after the shooting testified that at no time did Jackson point his rifle at anyone, and he was very sure about that.

An ERT member did report that he heard one, and possibly two members shout 'stop, drop your weapon', and at the same time he saw Jackson run up to the edge of a steep ravine. He testified that Jackson stopped, turned, and appeared to be raising his rifle as he turned when several rapid-fire shots rang out and Jackson dropped to the ground.

But under cross-examination the victim's family lawyer pointed out two years ago in this officer's written statement this officer said Jackson was holding his rifle in one hand as he turned. There was no mention of the gun in two hands or even raised to a shoulder.

One ERT member testified late Wednesday and said he was standing only about five feet from the officer who fired the eight rounds, and he said he could not see any rifle at all and could see Jackson clearly.

"This one again in my opinion, points out the need for a civilian agency to investigate these deaths," said Cameron Ward, the Jackson family lawyer. "When you have the RCMP investigating an RCMP-caused death I think it makes it very difficult for all of us to try to ascertain the true facts, and so we're overdue in having the new office set up that will be tasked with investigating these types of events in the future."
For Jackson's family and friends this has been a heart-wrenching week, especially when they learned Jackson was shot in the back.

'It's gut-wrenching," said Jackson's uncle Aubrey Jackson. "And it's really difficult for me to maintain my composure to listen and observe first-hand the difficulty that my family is having in soliciting truth."
In a statement the RCMP asks the public not to pre-judge and to wait for all the facts.
